title: feat(ui): team mode shows every agent and its sessions in the sidebar

commit.messageHeadline: feat(ui): add roster-first Agents home
fix(ui): align agents e2e navigation with roster home
perf(ui): defer agent page copy and route setup
feat(ui): link the agent switcher to the Agents home
fix(ui): restore eager agent settings route loading
feat(ui): add optional sidebar agent roster
fix(ui): share roster activity between sidebar and Agents home
feat(ui): group sidebar sessions by agent in roster mode
refactor(ui): break sidebar session navigation import cycle
feat(ui): team mode hides Home, adds a "+" agent switcher, and scopes…
fix(ui): persist the pre-team agent scope per gateway
fix(ui): type route tests against the team-mode page contracts
fix(ui): expose agent ids on identity chips and assert them in e2e
feat(ui): team mode replaces the agent chip with a workspace header
feat(ui): agent-first team sidebar rows and indicators
fix(ui): keep team activity on stable compact session rows
improve(ui): keep agent creation in Settings
fix(ui): deduplicate trailing sidebar status indicators
test(ui): keep roster activity fixture updates immutable
fix(ui): share one default agent avatar across surfaces
fix(ui): polish team-mode session rows and group actions
test(ui): follow the New conversation label in e2e
fix(ui): keep team-mode titles and names readable
fix(ui): keep the product mark for the system agent avatar
fix(ui): keep configured image avatars beside chat replies
Revert "improve(ui): keep agent creation in Settings"
docs(ui): preserve current sidebar menu wording
chore(ui): merge main into sidebar roster
fix(ui): reconcile sidebar roster integration checks
fix(ui): align sidebar fixtures and identity e2e with main

Codex review: blocked before merge. _Reviewed September 12, 2026, 3:42 AM ET / 07:42 UTC (Revision 18)._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes Adds an optional team sidebar with grouped agent sessions, remembered page scope, shared activity loading, and consistent agent avatars across the Control UI. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 2 items remain** This PR still provides distinct value beyond the merged Agents home page. The prior concrete findings are addressed, and the reviewed preference handling supports clearing the earlier generic compatibility warning. No blocking defect was established. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `0d827127ca2f8e65a8157a31950d1d6624dddcd0` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Useful, well-supported UI work with inspected visual proof and resolved prior findings; no additional concrete repair was identified. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (screenshot): Inspected synthetic Control UI captures demonstrate chip/team presentation and the new agent menu through the declared sidebar-roster entrypoint. Scoped UI policy accepts this visual boundary proof; preference and replacement behavior also have focused coverage, while a live team deployment remains unclaimed. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (screenshot): Inspected synthetic Control UI captures demonstrate chip/team presentation and the new agent menu through the declared sidebar-roster entrypoint. Scoped UI policy accepts this visual boundary proof; preference and replacement behavior also have focused coverage, while a live team deployment remains unclaimed. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 9 items | Pinned introduction and latest revision: The local base-to-head file inventory confirms the introduced surface. The preceding-head diff encountered an unavailable Git blob; the exact GitHub commit endpoint independently showed that the latest commit changes only mock task fixtures and two E2E selectors.
Existing preferences remain compatible: Missing or invalid team-mode values resolve to chip mode. The added preference fields use the existing browser settings owner; tests cover old settings, explicit modes, and null versus unset remembered scope.
Scope restoration: Selection preserves the pre-team scope, including All agents, across chat navigation, preference reload, and gateway switching; disabling team mode restores it and clears the remembered value. The tests exercise the production selection capability and settings serialization. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Control UI turns Gateway agent identities and session activity into navigation and chat views. Team mode groups those existing sessions while keeping page filters separate from the agent owning the open conversation. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Gateway agents and sessions] --> B[Shared activity window] C[Browser preferences] --> D[Chip or team mode] B --> E[Grouped sidebar and Agents home] D --> E E --> F[Conversation navigation] D --> G[Shared page filter] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Review config compatibility** - Confirm compatibility and upgrade impact for the changed config or default surface before merge. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.
Agent review details ### Security None. ### PR surface PR surface statistics unavailable: the file list is incomplete. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Browser preference surface** | 3 added fields; team mode defaults off | Mode, remembered scope, and collapsed agents stay within the existing gateway-scoped browser settings owner. | | **Production versus test growth** | Production/tooling net +1797; tests/fixtures net +3316; docs net +58 | Production growth supports the stated grouped navigation and shared avatar behavior, with substantial lifecycle and interaction coverage. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `unknown-data-model-change: ui/src/pages/config/memory-page.ts`, `unknown-truncated-pull-files`. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep team mode opt-in, preserve existing browser preferences, and serve both roster views through the shared activity and session owners. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Not applicable to a feature proposal. The inspected captures demonstrate the new visual states, and source review confirms the prior replacement-props repair. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Extending existing selection, session, and avatar owners with an opt-in presentation mode is a maintainable fit; the reviewed old-preference and restoration paths address the earlier compatibility concern. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [347fce255982](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/347fce25598215278fb84d5c549f58b8628c36d7). ### Labels Label justifications: - `P2`: This is a useful optional multi-agent navigation improvement with a bounded Control UI surface. - `rating: 🐚 platinum hermit`: Overall readiness is 🐚 platinum hermit; proof is 🦞 diamond lobster and patch quality is 🐚 platinum hermit. - `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`: ClawSweeper has no concrete contributor-facing blocker left for this PR. Sufficient (screenshot): Inspected synthetic Control UI captures demonstrate chip/team presentation and the new agent menu through the declared sidebar-roster entrypoint. Scoped UI policy accepts this visual boundary proof; preference and replacement behavior also have focused coverage, while a live team deployment remains unclaimed. - `proof: sufficient`: Contributor real behavior proof is sufficient. Inspected synthetic Control UI captures demonstrate chip/team presentation and the new agent menu through the declared sidebar-roster entrypoint. Scoped UI policy accepts this visual boundary proof; preference and replacement behavior also have focused coverage, while a live team deployment remains unclaimed. - `proof: 📸 screenshot`: Contributor real behavior proof includes screenshot evidence. Inspected synthetic Control UI captures demonstrate chip/team presentation and the new agent menu through the declared sidebar-roster entrypoint. Scoped UI policy accepts this visual boundary proof; preference and replacement behavior also have focused coverage, while a live team deployment remains unclaimed. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Pinned introduction and latest revision:** The local base-to-head file inventory confirms the introduced surface. The preceding-head diff encountered an unavailable Git blob; the exact GitHub commit endpoint independently showed that the latest commit changes only mock task fixtures and two E2E selectors. ([0d827127ca2f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0d827127ca2f8e65a8157a31950d1d6624dddcd0)) - **Existing preferences remain compatible:** Missing or invalid team-mode values resolve to chip mode. The added preference fields use the existing browser settings owner; tests cover old settings, explicit modes, and null versus unset remembered scope. ([`ui/src/app/settings.sidebar-prefs.node.test.ts:16`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0d827127ca2f8e65a8157a31950d1d6624dddcd0/ui/src/app/settings.sidebar-prefs.node.test.ts#L16), [0d827127ca2f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0d827127ca2f8e65a8157a31950d1d6624dddcd0)) - **Scope restoration:** Selection preserves the pre-team scope, including All agents, across chat navigation, preference reload, and gateway switching; disabling team mode restores it and clears the remembered value. The tests exercise the production selection capability and settings serialization. ([`ui/src/app/agent-selection.test.ts:109`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0d827127ca2f8e65a8157a31950d1d6624dddcd0/ui/src/app/agent-selection.test.ts#L109), [0d827127ca2f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0d827127ca2f8e65a8157a31950d1d6624dddcd0)) - **Prior plugin replacement finding resolved:** The host supplies session-list replacement props directly from the session owner before choosing its default renderer. The replacement regression covers chip-to-team-to-chip transitions and subsequent session updates without mounting the built-in list. Merged via squash.

- Prepared head SHA: [0d827127ca2f8e65a8157a31950d1d6624dddcd0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/141476/commits/0d827127ca2f8e65a8157a31950d1d6624dddcd0)
- Landed commit: [8c2996e01303dee2e0602d0617fbebea436c5ebe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8c2996e01303dee2e0602d0617fbebea436c5ebe)

<!-- openclaw-merge:5babee52-4d71-4105-b99a-943b9578a166 -->

Post-merge field report from a real multi-agent deployment:

We tested the merged Team Mode implementation with 10 agents and several hundred sessions, including one agent with hundreds of historical sessions.

What worked well:

- “Show all agents” displayed every agent with independently collapsible session lists.
- Bespoke sessions remained accessible without globally switching the UI into another agent's context.
- Opening sessions across several agents preserved Team Mode.
- Agent/session running indicators and collapsed-agent unread summaries updated correctly.
- Per-agent pagination prevented high-volume agents from overwhelming the sidebar.
- Split panes safely retained multiple bespoke chats belonging to different agents.

This fills the PR's noted gap that no live team deployment had been exercised. The merged feature solves the core cross-agent navigation problem we were trying to address.

We found one filtering bug and one follow-up workflow opportunity and are filing each separately to keep them focused:

- Heartbeat sessions classified as `kind: other` bypass the System and Automation session filters.
- A global cross-agent Watchlist, independent of agent-specific pins, would provide one compact list of actively monitored sessions.

We also prototyped and live-tested both fixes/extensions locally against this branch. Thanks for moving this forward—the resulting multi-agent view is already substantially more useful for real operations.
